text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk: U.S. ready for dialogue with Iran.
- Cable TV providers refusing to hook up some areas.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: No Har Homa deals.
- No-confidence motions fail.
- Palestinian Authority official: Israel lacing gum with aphrodisiac.
- Channel 1 journalist Amnon Abramovitch probed under warning.
- Government: El Al sale plan to be published next week.
- Howard Johnson hotels establish Israel presence.
- Plastics manufacturer Plasson mulls third attempt at IPO.
- Zim slips into red; Clal Industries net sharply down.
- Interest rates left unchanged.
GLOBES
- Prime minister's office, Treasury and Bank of Israel in contacts for economic package deal including budget cuts and foreign currency liberalisation.
- Sharp drop of 21 percent in building starts in first quarter.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu ahead of summit with Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak: I'll not come empty-handed.
- New times: Proposal to impose .5 percent tax on import of foreign currency.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH

- Compromise being drafted whereby (1) Once infrastructure is laid on Har Homa, work is stopped, (2) Infrastructure work begins for Arab neighbourhood of Har Homa B, and (3) Simultaneous construction of two neighbourhoods Arab and Jewish.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon asks that land not be sold to Arabs who are not residents of Israel.
HAARETZ
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat: Construction for Arabs is no alternative for halting the construction of Jewish settlements.
- Netanyahu will decide in dispute on continued foreign currency reform between Treasury and Bank of Israel.
